text:
nina: quick take — instead of CP RPC per request, how about a gossip-style assertion distribution to regional proxies? small blurb, please react.
sam: sounds promising. main risk = longer tail to revoke. need short TTLs + revocation markers.
raju: we tried gossip (pub/sub over replication stream) in a small test. pros: no central hot CP during surge. cons: you must design for eventual consistency and revoked assertions may linger ~several seconds.
megan: legal: lingering is fine if auditable. requirement: every served request must log assertion id + key id + local timestamp. customers must be able to query exports.
nina: ops: how do proxies detect that an assertion is stale but still being honored?
raju: add a short-lived local flag when revocation seen: proxies mark "LRU-revoke" and start rejecting new sessions unless tenant opted into failover. also emit metric `assertion_revoked_but_used`.
sam: implementation tips: - TTL 30-90s - jittered refresh - signed assertion with kid - include `fallback_policy` field (deny | allow-with-flag) - keep payload <1kb to fit headers.
megan: keys: we need key rotation mapping and tying signing events to a ticket id in KMS logs. add `kid` and also `sign_ticket` in audit DB.
nina: what about clock skew across regions causing early expiry?
raju: use a skew window (±5s) and grace TTL after exp (configurable per-tenant). but favour short expiry for fast revocation.
sam: also add an emergency revoke that sets a global revocation marker in the replication stream — proxies subscribe and apply immediately. keep that path reliable (SLA + alerting).
megan: customers will want notifications for failover events. propose an event stream mapping request windows to assertion ids we can share.
nina: ok action items: sam write RFC for gossip vs CP-push tradeoffs; raju to add prototype with revocation marker; megan to capture compliance export schema; i'll schedule sync next Tue.
